name: awesome-artificial-intelligence-regulation
desc: This repository aims to map the ecosystem of artificial intelligence guidelines, principles, codes of ethics, standards, regulation and beyond.

resources.name: Artificial Intelligence Mission Austria 2030
resources.desc: Shaping the Future of Artificial Intelligence in Austria. The Austrian ministry for Innovation and Technology published their vision for AI until 2030.

resources.name: Brazilian AI Regulation (PL 2338/2023)
resources.desc: A proposed bill in Brazil aiming to establish a comprehensive framework for the development and use of artificial intelligence, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and alignment with international standards.

resources.name: Artificial Intelligence and Data Act (AIDA)
resources.desc: An Act to enact the Consumer Privacy Protection Act, the Personal Information and Data Protection Tribunal Act and the Artificial Intelligence and Data Act and to make consequential and related amendments to other Acts

resources.name: Beijing AI Principles
resources.desc: initiative for the research, development, use, governance and long-term planning of AI, calling for its healthy development to support the construction of a human community with a shared future, and the realization of beneficial AI for humankind and nature.

resources.name: China Internet Security Law
resources.desc: China's law which enacted to increase cybersecurity and national security, safeguard cyberspace sovereignty and public interest, protect the legitimate rights and interests of citizens, legal persons and other organisations, and promote healthy economic and social development (and was argued by the Chinese ministry for industry and information that this law justified the means of pursuing the "Going Out" strategy China has persisted on ever since 1999). KPMG's summary of the Cybersecurity Law. Center for strategic & international studies overview of China's new Data Privacy law

resources.name: China's Administrative Provisions on Information Services on Microblogs
resources.desc: China's provisions which require microblogging sites (social media sites) to obtain relevant credentials by law, verify users' real identities, establish mechanisms for dispelling and refuting rumors, etc. Summary of rules by the US Law Library of Congress.

resources.name: China's Interim Measures for the Management of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services
resources.desc: The first administrative regulation on the management of Generative AI services, which came into effect on August 15, 2023.

resources.name: China's Personal Information Security Specification (Translation)
resources.desc: The Chinese Government's first major digital privacy rules which took effect in May 2018, which lays out granular guidelines for consent and how personal data should be collected, used and shared. Center for strategic & international studies overview of the specification

resources.name: Decision on strengthening the protection of online information
resources.desc: The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (NPC) of the People's Republic of China adopted the decision on strengthening the protection of online information - this is an act that contains 12 clauses applicable to entities both in the public and private sectors in respect to the collection and processing of electronic personal information on the internet.

resources.name: Personal Data Protection Act
resources.desc: The personal data protection act of the Republic of China, which is enacted to regulate the collection, processing and use of personal data as so to prevent harm on personality rights, and to facilitate the proper use of personal data.

resources.name: Smart Dubai Artificial Intelligence Principles and Ethics - Ethical AI Toolkit
resources.desc: created to provide practical help across a city ecosystem. It supports industry, academia and individuals in understanding how AI systems can be used responsibly. It consists of principles and guidelines, and a self-assessment tool for developers to assess their platforms.

resources.name: Annex III Deep Classifier
resources.desc: AI-powered classifier mapping product features to EU AI Act Annex III high-risk categories (items 1-8) plus Article 50 transparency obligations, with Article 26(6) deployer audit-trail considerations.

resources.name: Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy AI
resources.desc: European Commission document prepared by the High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (AI HLEG).

resources.name: EU AI Act
resources.desc: The EU Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act is a legal framework that regulates AI in the European Union; this was the first regulation implemented on AI (overview).

resources.name: EU AI Act + ISO 42001 + NIST AI RMF Crosswalk
resources.desc: Deterministic mapping between EU AI Act Articles, ISO/IEC 42001:2023 Clauses, NIST AI RMF Functions, Colorado SB 24-205, and GDPR Article 22 — triple-framework alignment for compliance teams.

resources.name: EU AI Act Governance Assessment Example (DE)
resources.desc: Internal governance and assessment document template in German — community-suggested resource per #33.

resources.name: EU AI Act Penalty Calculator
resources.desc: Penalty estimator covering EU AI Act fines under Article 99 (operator obligations) and Article 101 (general-purpose AI (GPAI) provider sanctions), with tiers depending on type of infringement and annual worldwide turnover.

resources.name: eucomplyhub
resources.desc: Open methodology and interactive tooling covering EU AI Act audit workflows (Annex III classification, GPAI Article 53, Article 50 transparency) and ISO/IEC 42001:2023 crosswalk.

resources.name: GDPR.EU Guide
resources.desc: A project co-funded by the Horizon 2020 Framework programme of the EU which provides a resource for organisations and individuals researching GDPR, including a library of straightforward and up-to-date information to help organisations achieve GDPR compliance (Legal Text).

resources.name: General Data Protection Regulation GDPR
resources.desc: Legal text for the EU GDPR regulation 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016 on the protection of natural persons with regard to the processing of personal data and on the free movement of such data, and repealing Directive 95/46/EC

resources.name: SetAIComply
resources.desc: EU AI Act compliance workspace for European SMEs, covering applicability, Annex III risk classification, Annex IV technical documentation and DPIAs, localised in all 24 EU languages; includes a public risk-tier checker of 15 questions across Article 5 prohibited practices, Annex III high-risk uses and Article 50 transparency triggers, evaluated client-side with no signup.

resources.name: IT Amendment Rules, 2026
resources.desc: These are updated rules that amend the IT Rules, 2021 to further strengthen due diligence framework for intermediaries, particularly in relation to synthetically generated information (SGI) and associated online harms. Frequently asked questions here.

resources.name: The Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act
resources.desc: India's DPDP Act aims to provide for the processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognises both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process such personal data for lawful purposes and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto. The DPDP Act was passed in the Parliament of India in August 2023 and it's implementation is being driven by MeitY, which has released draft rules based on the act for public consultation on 3rd January 2025. The draft DPDP rules are available for public review and feedback here.

resources.name: The National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence
resources.desc: The approach in this paper focuses on how India can leverage the transformative technologies to ensure social and inclusive growth in line with the development philosophy of the government. In addition, India should strive to replicate these solutions in other similarly placed developing countries.

resources.name: The Principles for Responsible AI
resources.desc: The paper incorporates insights, feedback and experiences consolidated through inter-ministerial consultations, large-scale global multi-stakeholder consultations and a series of 1-1 consultations with AI ethics experts in India and globally, as well as wider public consultations, conducted over the last 15 months. This paper is meant to serve as an essential roadmap for the AI ecosystem, encouraging adoption of AI in a responsible manner in India and building public trust in the use of this technology, placing the idea of 'AI for All' at its very core.

resources.name: National AI Strategy of Ireland
resources.desc: Ireland releases their national AI strategy in 2026 tackling literacy, infrastructure, adoption, etc.

resources.name: The principles of the policy for the responsible development of the field of AI
resources.desc: The draft policy for regulation and ethics in the field of artificial intelligence, with an emphasis on "responsible innovation", is intended to ensure the advancement of the industry while safeguarding the public interest

resources.name: Artificial Intelligence National Agenda Proposal for Mexico
resources.desc: Recommendations for multi-faceted commitment to guide the development and use of artificial intelligence in Mexico in an ethical and responsible manner.

resources.name: Data Protection Act 2012
resources.desc: The Personal Data Protection Act 2012 (the "Act") sets out the law on data protection in Singapore. Apart from establishing a general data protection regime, the Act also regulates telemarketing practices.

resources.name: Protection from Online Falsehoods and Manipulation Act 2019
resources.desc: An act to prevent the electronic communication in Singapore of false statements of fact, to suppress support for and counteract the effects of such communication, to safeguard against the use of online accounts for such communication and for information manipulation, to enable measures to be taken to enhance transparency of online political advertisements and for related matters.

resources.name: New Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP)
resources.desc: The New Federal Act on Data Protection (nFADP) was passed in the Swiss Parliament in 2020 and came into effect from September 1, 2023. It aims to improve the processing of personal data and grant new rights to the people concerned, and also comes with a number of obligations for companies. Every company, Swiss or otherwise, offering goods and services to Swiss citizens and processing their personal data is subject to the nFADP. More highlights on nFADP available here.

resources.name: UAE National Strategy for AI
resources.desc: This paper outlines the UAE's ambitions to become a fast adopter of emerging AI technologies across Government, as well as attract top AI talent to experiment with new technologies and work in a sophisticated, secure ecosystem to solve complex problems.

resources.name: The Information Commissioner's Office guide to Data Protection
resources.desc: This guide is for data protection officers and others who have day-to-day responsibility for data protection. It is aimed at small and medium-sized organisations, but it may be useful for larger organisations too.

resources.name: UK Data Protection Act of 2018
resources.desc: The DPA 2018 enacts the GDPR into UK Law, however in doing so has included various "derogations" as permitted by the GDPR, resulting in some key differenced (which although small are not of insignificance impact and may have a greater impact after Brexit).

resources.name: UK's AI regulation: a pro-innovation approach
resources.desc: This white paper details the UK's plans for implementing a pro-innovation approach to AI regulation.

resources.name: AI Laws by State
resources.desc: Free 50-state tracker for U.S. artificial intelligence legislation, sourced from primary state legislature feeds. Covers bill status, effective dates, penalty structures, and topic categorization (deepfakes, hiring, healthcare AI, disclosure, bias audits).

resources.name: California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA)
resources.desc: Legal text for California's consumer privacy act

resources.name: DoD's Ethical Principles for AI
resources.desc: The U.S.A. Department of Defense responsible AI guidelines for tech contractors. The guidelines provide a step-by-step process to follow during the planning, development, and deployment phases of the technical lifecycle.

resources.name: EU-U.S. and Swiss-U.S. Privacy Shield Frameworks
resources.desc: The EU-U.S. and Swiss-U.S. Privacy Shield Frameworks were designed by the U.S. Department of Commerce and the European Commission and Swiss Administration to provide companies on both sides of the Atlantic with a mechanism to comply with data protection requirements when transferring personal data from the European Union and Switzerland to the United States in support of transatlantic commerce.

resources.name: Executive Order on Maintaining American Leadership in AI
resources.desc: Official mandate by the President of the US to

resources.name: Fair Credit Reporting Act 2018
resources.desc: The Fair Reporting Act is a federal law that regulates the collection of consumers' credit information and access to their credit reports.

resources.name: Gramm-Leach-Billey Act (for financial institutions)
resources.desc: The Graham-Leach-Billey Act requires financial institutions (companies that offer consumers financial projects or services like loans, financial, or investment advice, or insurance) to explain their information-sharing practices to their customers and to safeguard sensitive data.

resources.name: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act of 1996
resources.desc: The HIPAA required the secretary of the US department of health and human services (HHS) to develop regulations protecting the privacy and security of certain health information, which then HHS published what is known as the HIPAA Privacy Rule, and the HIPAA Security Rule.

resources.name: Privacy Act of 1974
resources.desc: The privacy act of 1974 which establishes a code of fair information practices that governs the collection, maintenance, use and dissemination of information about individuals that is maintained in systems of records by federal agencies.

resources.name: Privacy Protection Act of 1980
resources.desc: The Privacy Protection Act of 1980 protects journalists from being required to turn over to law enforcement any work product and documentary materials, including sources, before it is disseminated to the public.

resources.name: The White House Executive Order in AI
resources.desc: The USA Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence

resources.name: U.S. AI Policy Tracker (USASI)
resources.desc: Independent tracker of 30 U.S. federal AI laws, executive orders, OMB memoranda, standards, and plans, newest first. Each entry summarizes what the document says in its own terms, gives its current status (in effect, revoked, or superseded) from official sources, and links to the official text.

resources.name: AI & Machine Learning 8 principles for Responsible ML
resources.desc: The Institute for Ethical AI & Machine Learning has put together 8 principles for responsible machine learning that are to be adopted by individuals and delivery teams designing, building and operating machine learning systems.

resources.name: AI Governance Engineering: The Thesis & Body of Knowledge
resources.desc: A practitioner-oriented Thesis and Body of Knowledge treating AI governance as an engineering discipline (policy-as-code, agent registries, eval gates, runtime guardrails, machine-readable evidence) rather than a documentation exercise, by Jorge García Aibar and Aurélie Pols.

resources.name: Algorithm charter for Aotearoa New Zealand
resources.desc: The Algorithm Charter for Aotearoa New Zealand is an evolving piece of work that needs to respond to emerging technologies and also be fit-for-purpose for government agencies.

resources.name: An Evaluation of Guidelines - The Ethics of Ethics
resources.desc: A research paper that analyses multiple Ethics principles

resources.name: Association for Computer Machinery's Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct
resources.desc: This is the code of ethics that has been put together in 1992 by the Association for Computer Machinery and updated in 2018. The Code is designed to inspire and guide the ethical conduct of all computing professionals, including current and aspiring practitioners, instructors, students, influencers, and anyone who uses computing technology in an impactful way. Additionally, the Code serves as a basis for remediation when violations occur. The Code includes principles formulated as statements of responsibility, based on the understanding that the public good is always the primary consideration.

resources.name: Boundary & Consent Reference Frameworks
resources.desc: For reference only. Defines non-execution judgment boundaries and consent-state gating for AI systems.

resources.name: Declaration for responsible and intelligent data practice
resources.desc: a shared vision of what best practice in data looks like by Open Data Manchester.

resources.name: European Commission's Guidelines for Trustworthy AI
resources.desc: The Ethics Guidelines for Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence (AI) is a document prepared by the High-Level Expert Group on Artificial Intelligence (AI HLEG). This independent expert group was set up by the European Commission in June 2018, as part of the AI strategy announced earlier that year.

resources.name: From What to How: An initial review of publicly available AI Ethics Tools, Methods and Research to translate principles into practices
resources.desc: A paper published by the UK Digital Catapult that aims to identify and present the gap between principles and their practical applications.

resources.name: IEEE's Ethically Aligned Design
resources.desc: A Vision for Prioritizing Human Wellbeing with Artificial Intelligence and Autonomous Systems that encourages technologists to prioritize ethical considerations in the creation of autonomous and intelligent technologies.

resources.name: Montreal AI Ethics Institute State of AI Ethics June 2020 Report
resources.desc: A resource put together by the Montreal AI Ethics Institute that captures the most relevant research and reporting in the domain of AI ethics between March 2020 and June 2020.

resources.name: Montréal Declaration for a responsible development of artificial intelligence
resources.desc: ethical principles and values that promote the fundamental interests of people and group created as an initiative by Université de Montréal

resources.name: Oxford's Recommendations for AI Governance
resources.desc: A set of recommendations from Oxford's Future of Humanity institute which focus on the infrastructure and attributes required for efficient design, development, and research around the ongoing work building & implementing AI standards.

resources.name: PWC's Responsible AI
resources.desc: PWC has put together a survey and a set of principles that abstract some of the key areas they've identified for responsible AI.

resources.name: Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
resources.desc: The Recommendation by the UNESCO is a comprehensive international framework aiming to shape the development and use of AI technologies and establishes a set of values in line with the promotion and protection of human rights, human dignity, and environmental sustainability. It has been adopted by acclamation by 193 Member States at UNESCO's General Conference in November 2021. For more information, refer to UNESCO's 2023 publication on key facts here.

resources.name: SHELET Protocol
resources.desc: A structured governance loop (Sense → Hypothesize → Elect → Let → Evaluate → Tighten) for human oversight of AI systems, emphasizing sovereignty through iterative compression rather than rigid control. Source

resources.name: Singapore Data Protection Govt Commission's AI Governance Principles
resources.desc: The Singapore government's Personal Data Protection Commission has put together a set of guiding principles towards data protection and human involvement in automated systems, and comes with a report that breaks down the guiding principles and motivations.

resources.name: Technical and Organizational Best Practices
resources.desc: A resource put together by Foundation for Best Practices in Machine Learning (FBPML) with technical guidelines (e.g. fairness and non-discrimination, monitoring and maintenance, data quality, product traceability, explainability) and organizational guidelines (e.g. data governance, product management, human resources management, compliance and auditing). Community contributions are welcome via the FBPML Wiki.

resources.name: Toronto Declaration
resources.desc: Protecting the right to equality and non-discrimination in machine learning systems by accessnow.

resources.name: UK Government's Data Ethics Framework Principles
resources.desc: A resource put together by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) which outlines an overview of data ethics, together with a 7-principle framework.

resources.name: Understanding artificial intelligence ethics and safety
resources.desc: A guide for the responsible design and implementation of AI systems in the public sector by David Leslie from the Alan Turing Institute.

resources.name: YRproject
resources.desc: Free trilingual (EN/NL/DE) knowledge base on EU AI regulation with practical self-assessment scans that map which AI Act obligations apply to your organisation.

resources.name: ACS Code of Professional Conduct - PDF
resources.desc: Australian ICT (Information and Communication Technology) sector professional organization.

resources.name: ai-governance.json
resources.desc: An open specification (Draft v0.1, CC BY 4.0) for publishing a machine-readable manifest of an organization's AI governance facts at a well-known path - presence-only, date-stamped, self-hosted. Stewarded by Certian.

resources.name: IEEE Global Initiative for Ethical Considerations in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Systems (AS)
resources.desc: IEEE Approved Standards Projects specifically focused on the Ethically Aligned Design principles, and includes 14 (P700X) standards which cover topics from data collection to privacy, to algorithmic bias and beyond.

resources.name: ISO/IEC's Standards for Artificial Intelligence
resources.desc: The ISO's initiative for Artificial Intelligence standards, which include a large set of subsequent standards ranging across Big Data, AI Terminology, Machine Learning frameworks, etc.

resources.name: Open Ethics Transparency Protocol
resources.desc: The Open Ethics Transparency Protocol (OETP or Protocol) describes the creation and exchange of voluntary ethics Disclosures for products that involve Automated Decision-Making (ADM), including AI-powered services, Robotic process automation (RPA) tools, and robots. It is brought as a solution to increase the transparency of how digital products with full or partial automation are built and deployed.

resources.name: ADMT Checker
resources.desc: Free, no-signup tool that shows whether California's CCPA rules on automated decisionmaking technology (ADMT) apply to a business's systems, which consumer rights attach (pre-use notice, opt-out, access, appeal), and when each obligation starts (1 January 2027 for ADMT already in use). The same facts are published as an open CC BY 4.0 JSON dataset tied to sections of the CPPA regulations. Not legal advice.

resources.name: Aequitas' Bias & Fairness Audit Toolkit
resources.desc: The Bias Report is powered by Aequitas, an open-source bias audit toolkit for machine learning developers, analysts, and policymakers to audit machine learning models for discrimination and bias, and make informed and equitable decisions around developing and deploying predictive risk-assessment tools.

resources.name: AI Act Classifier
resources.desc: MIT-licensed npm package and CLI that maps a plain-text AI system description to EU AI Act Article 5, Annex III, Article 50 and GPAI provisions with EUR-Lex citations (English and German, deterministic keyword rules, not legal advice). Also available as a GitHub Action for CI and as a free web version.

resources.name: AI Agent Incident Register
resources.desc: A free, numbered public register of AI agent incidents, each analysed for legal liability: the duty engaged, how liability allocates across the deployer/shared/vendor chain, and the preventative governance step, mapped to OWASP ASI, NIST AI RMF, IMDA and the EU AI Act.

resources.name: AI Atlas Nexus
resources.desc: An open-source Python toolkit from IBM Research that uses knowledge graphs to unify AI risk taxonomies (NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10, EU AI Act, MIT AI Risk Repository) for risk identification, prioritization, and compliance automation. Listed in the OECD AI Catalogue and part of the AI Alliance Trust & Safety initiative.

resources.name: AI Disclosure Kit
resources.desc: Hosted SaaS that generates EU AI Act Article 50 disclosure text (chatbots, synthetic content, emotion/biometric, deepfakes) in 10 EU languages with exact clause citations. Free tier available.

resources.name: AI Governance Compare
resources.desc: A source-traceable comparison of how the European Union and China regulate AI and data: one question per note (AI content labelling, personal data, cross-border data transfers, platform responsibility, AI liability), where every claim carries an official source (EUR-Lex, CAC and others), an evidence grade (A/B/C) and the date it was last checked. Around thirty notes in English and Chinese, plus an agent skill that reads the same corpus instead of answering from memory; external links are re-checked weekly by CI. Not legal advice.

resources.name: AI Law Radar
resources.desc: A free, primary-sourced tracker of AI-regulation obligations and deadlines across 13 jurisdictions: interactive map, dated register, open data (CC BY 4.0), a REST API + MCP server, calendar/CSV export, and an embeddable widget. Re-verified daily; not legal advice.

resources.name: AI Policy Generator
resources.desc: Free browser-local tool that creates an editable workplace AI acceptable-use policy DOCX without signup, uploads, or an AI model.

resources.name: AIR Blackbox
resources.desc: Open-source EU AI Act compliance scanner and trust layer for Python AI agents. Checks code against Articles 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, and 15 with framework-specific integrations for LangChain, CrewAI, AutoGen, OpenAI, and Anthropic SDKs. Includes HMAC-SHA256 audit chains, PII tokenization, consent gating, and prompt injection detection. Apache 2.0 licensed.

resources.name: Alibi
resources.desc: An open-source Python library for machine learning model inspection and interpretation.

resources.name: Allowly Hiring Evidence
resources.desc: A hosted deterministic policy runner for structured employment screening that records decisions under an approved policy and exports Hiring Decision Packs with signed records; its AI-assisted hiring use case maps where those records can support EU AI Act and GDPR review and states what they do not prove.

resources.name: Awesome Machine Learning Production List
resources.desc: A list of tools and frameworks that support the design, development and operation of production machine learning systems, currently maintained by The Institute for Ethical AI & Machine Learning.

resources.name: Cape Python
resources.desc: Easily apply privacy-enhancing techniques for data science and machine learning tasks in Pandas and Spark. Can be used in conjunction with Cape Core to collaborate on privacy policies and distribute those policies for data projects across teams and organizations.

resources.name: Certian
resources.desc: A free, independent register of AI governance facts: date-stamped, primary-sourced records of AI disclosure laws across jurisdictions, the EU Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content and its signatories, and an Article 50 screener, with a public changelog recording every change to the record.

resources.name: Council of AI
resources.desc: Independent measurement of AI models and the MCP servers they use, published on a signed board with signed records anyone can re-check for free (measurement, not certification). Live totals: https://councilof.ai/api/gspc; dataset DOI 10.57967/hf/10114; free MCP server ai.councilof/gspc-free.

resources.name: Deployer AI Risk Register (DARR)
resources.desc: An open catalogue of canonical AI risks for organizations that deploy AI systems, consolidated from the MIT AI Risk Repository and crosswalked to ISO/IEC 42001, the EU AI Act, and MITRE ATLAS. Open data (CC BY 4.0); source and dataset on GitHub.

resources.name: Dutybound AI Regulation Deadlines
resources.desc: An open dataset (CC BY 4.0, JSON and CSV, synced daily) of AI-regulation obligations under the EU AI Act as amended by the Digital Omnibus, Poland's AI Systems Act, South Korea's AI Basic Act and US state laws, each with its date, scope, expected evidence and source; browsable at getdutybound.com/deadlines.

resources.name: EU AI Act Check
resources.desc: A free, German-language interactive check that classifies an AI system into the EU AI Act risk classes (prohibited, high-risk, limited, minimal) and lists the key resulting obligations. Runs entirely in the browser; not legal advice.

resources.name: eXplainability Toolbox
resources.desc: The Institute for Ethical AI & Machine Learning proposal for an extended version of the traditional data science process which focuses on algorithmic bias and explainability, to ensure a baseline of risks around undesired biases can be mitigated.

resources.name: FAT Forensics
resources.desc: A Python toolkit for evaluating Fairness, Accountability and Transparency of Artificial Intelligence systems. It is built on top of SciPy and NumPy, and distributed under the 3-Clause BSD license (new BSD).

resources.name: IBM's AI Explainability 360 Open Source Toolkit
resources.desc: This is IBM's toolkit that includes large number of examples, research papers and demos implementing several algorithms that provide insights on fairness in machine learning systems.

resources.name: Linux Foundation AI Landscape
resources.desc: The official list of tools in the AI landscape curated by the Linux Foundation, which contains well maintained and used tools and frameworks.

resources.name: Made by Human
resources.desc: A self-disclosure labeling system for transparent human-AI collaboration in creative work. Provides open-source SVG badges (Made by Human, Co-created with AI, Crafted by Human, Human in the Loop) for projects to signal whether they are entirely human-made, AI-assisted, or AI-collaborative.

resources.name: Microsoft Fairlearn
resources.desc: An open-source toolkit for assessing and improving fairness in machine learning products developed by Microsoft

resources.name: Microsoft Interpret ML
resources.desc: An open-source toolkit for improving explainability/interpretability developed by Microsoft

resources.name: Open Ethics Data Passport
resources.desc: The Open Ethics Data Passport (OEDP) is focused on describing the origins of the models by sheding light on how the training datasets were collected, cleaned, labeled, and used for training of the AI models.

resources.name: Open Ethics Label: AI nutrition labels
resources.desc: Open Ethics Label (OEL) is a "nutrition label" for digital products, including AI systems. It brings standard of self-disclosure to digital products to make these products transparent and safe for consumers.

resources.name: Orca AI Incident Archive
resources.desc: An open database of real-world AI agent security incidents (354 records, 2025-01 to 2026-09, including 70 agent-specific policy and regulation records), each with at least one primary source and fields that separate confirmed harm from researcher demonstrations. Open data (CC BY 4.0) with JSON and CSV exports.

resources.name: OrcaPromptVault
resources.desc: An open archive of the system prompts and tool-call schemas that shipped AI products actually send, one directory per product and dated, with each artifact labelled as captured off the wire or reported by the vendor. Gives a transparency or disclosure review something to check a vendor statement against. Open source (AGPL-3.0), sources cited per artifact.

resources.name: Orchard Kit
resources.desc: Alignment, safety & cognitive architecture for autonomous AI agents. Membrane security, epistemic tagger, self-audit, agent discovery, cognitive architecture, collective cognition. Zero dependencies.

resources.name: PrivacyScrubber
resources.desc: A 100% client-side Zero-Trust Data Sanitization (ZTDS) tool and open-source MCP runtime guard (privacyscrubber-mcp) that redacts customer PII, protected health information (PHI), and sensitive credentials in local memory with zero network egress before prompt transmission to AI models, supporting EU AI Act, GDPR, and HIPAA compliance.

resources.name: Responsible AI Studio
resources.desc: Free and low-cost tools that generate jurisdiction-aware AI governance documents — AI usage policies, risk registers, DPAs, incident-response playbooks, and EU AI Act / NIST AI RMF gap analyses — across 14 industries and 14 jurisdictions. Includes a free AI readiness score and a data study mapping 378 AI-relevant laws. Sample outputs are viewable before purchase.

resources.name: Signato AI Act Readiness Quiz
resources.desc: Free 2-minute self-assessment of EU AI Act exposure for HR and compliance teams.

resources.name: Taking action on digital ethics
resources.desc: from Avanade

resources.name: TinyTools
resources.desc: Free browser-based utilities for AI compliance and transparency, including an EU AI Act compliant AI content disclosure generator (Article 50), AI robots.txt generator, and AI cost calculator. No signup required. Open source.

resources.name: TrustHawk
resources.desc: Free public ratings of 150+ AI companies on safety, transparency, security and privacy, built from verified public sources, with every score linked to its source.

resources.name: Where Do My Prompts Go?
resources.desc: A free, sourced tracker of how 25 AI tools and APIs handle user data: training on prompts, default retention, zero data retention (ZDR), abuse-monitoring exceptions, data residency, SOC 2 / ISO 27001 and HIPAA BAAs. Every value quotes and links the vendor's own policy page with a check date, and fields no official page states are marked "unverified". Open data in JSON and CSV; a nightly job re-fetches the sources. Not legal advice.

resources.name: AI Governance Certifications Compared
resources.desc: Comparison by AI Course Check of the IAPP AIGP and ISACA AI governance certifications, covering who can take each exam, price and validity, with links to the issuers' own pages.

resources.name: Bias and Discrimination in AI
resources.desc: Free course by the University of Montreal and IVADO (via edX) about the discriminatory effects of algorithmic decision-making and responsible machine learning (institutional and technical strategies to identify and address bias).

resources.name: Data science ethics
resources.desc: Free course by Prof. Jagadish from the University of Michigan (via Coursera) that covers data ownership, privacy and anonymity, data validity, and algorithmic fairness.

resources.name: Intro to AI ethics
resources.desc: Free course by Kaggle introducing the base concepts of ethics in AI and how to mitigate related problems.

resources.name: Introduction to AI Safety, Ethics, and Society
resources.desc: Developed by Dan Hendrycks, director of the Center for AI Safety, this free online textbook aims to provide an accessible introduction to students, practitioners and others looking to better understand issues pertaining to AI Safety and Ethics. Apart from online reading, this book is available as a PDF here and also as a free virtual course here.

resources.name: ISO 42001 Visual Library
resources.desc: A visual learning library for ISO/IEC 42001. Helps people understand, remember, and communicate the standard through reference cards, infographics, memory cards, and Annex A domain summaries.

resources.name: Practical Data Ethics
resources.desc: Free course by Rachel Thomas from the University of San Francisco Data Institute (via fast.ai) that covers disinformation, bias and fairness, foundations of ethics, privacy and surveillance, algorithmic colonialism

resources.name: Udacity's Secure & Private AI Course
resources.desc: Free course by Udacity which introduces three cutting-edge technologies for privacy-preserving AI: Federated Learning, Differential Privacy, and Encrypted Computation.

resources.name: AI RFX Procurement Framework
resources.desc: A procurement framework for evaluating the maturity of machine learning systems put together by cross functional teams of academics, industry practitioners and technical individuals at The Institute for Ethical AI & Machine Learning to empower industry practitioners looking to procure machine learning suppliers.

resources.name: Checklist for data science projects
resources.desc: Deon by DrivenData is a command line tool that allows you to easily add an ethics checklist to your data science projects.

resources.name: Designing Ethical AI Experiences Checklist and Agreement
resources.desc: document to guide the development of accountable, de-risked, respectful, secure, honest, and usable artificial intelligence (AI) systems with a diverse team aligned on shared ethics. Carnegie Mellon University, Software Engineering Institute.

resources.name: Ethical OS Toolkit
resources.desc: A toolkit that dives into 8 risk zones to assess the potential challenges that a technology team may face, together with 14 scenarios to provide examples, and 7 future-proofing strategies to help take ethical action.

resources.name: Ethics Canvas
resources.desc: A resource inspired by the traditional business canvas, which provides an interactive way to brainstorm potential risks, opportunities and solutions to ethical challenges that may be faced in a project using post-it note-like approach.

resources.name: FAIAS — Financial AI Independent Assurance Standard
resources.desc: An open baseline (CC BY 4.0) for reviewing generative, agentic and predictive AI systems in financial institutions: 109 review questions across nine domains, each with a review canvas, the evidence a reviewer should ask for, and a test procedure that runs outside production.

resources.name: Kat Zhou's Design Ethically Resources
resources.desc: A set of workshops that can be organised across teams to identify challenges, assess current risks and take action on potential issues around ethical challenges that may be faced.

resources.name: Machine Learning Assurance
resources.desc: Quick look at machine learning assurance: process of recording, understanding, verifying, and auditing machine learning models and their transactions.

resources.name: Markula Center's Ethical Toolkit for Engineering/Design Practice
resources.desc: A practical and comprehensible toolkit with seven components to aid practitioners reflect, and judge the moral grounds in which they are operating.

resources.name: ODEP's Checklist for Employers: Facilitating the Hiring of People with Disabilities Through the Use of eRecruiting Screening Systems, Including AI
resources.desc: The Employer Assistance and Resource Network on Disability Inclusion (EARN) and the Partnership on Employment & Accessible Technology (PEAT), which are both funded through the U.S. Department of Labor's Office of Disability Employment Policy (ODEP), collaborated on an inclusive AI checklist for employers. The checklist provides direction for leadership, human resources personnel, equal employment opportunity managers, and procurement officers for reviewing AI tools used in recruiting and candidate assessment for fairness and inclusion of individuals with disabilities.

resources.name: Open Ethics Maturity Model (OEMM)
resources.desc: The Open Ethics Maturity Model (OEMM) is a five-level framework. It embarks the organization on a journey toward transparent governance of AI and autonomous systems.

resources.name: San Francisco City's Ethics & Algorithms Toolkit
resources.desc: A risk management framework for government leaders and staff who work with algorithms, providing a two part assessment process including an algorithmic assessment process, and a process to address the risks.

resources.name: UK Government's Data Ethics Workbook
resources.desc: A resource put together by the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS) which provides a set of questions that can be asked by practitioners in the public sector, which address each of the principles in their Data Ethics Framework Principles.

resources.name: US NIST AI Risk Management Framework
resources.desc: The Framework is intended to help developers, users and evaluators of AI systems better manage AI risks which could affect individuals, organizations, society, or the environment.

resources.name: World Economic Forum's Guidelines for Procurement
resources.desc: The WEF has put together a set of guidelines for governments to be able to safely and reliably procure machine learning related systems, which has been trialled with the UK government.

resources.name: AI Safety Newsletter
resources.desc: A weekly newsletter from the Center for AI Safety providing updates on AI research, policy, and other areas for a non-technical audience.

resources.name: AI Weekly
resources.desc: Tracks what influential AI experts and organizations are reading and sharing, with ranked coverage of models, funding, policy and research.

resources.name: Import AI
resources.desc: A newsletter curated by OpenAI's Jack Clark which curates the most resent and relevant AI research, as well as relevant societal issues that intersect with technical AI research.

resources.name: Matt's thoughts in between
resources.desc: Newsletter curated by Entrepreneur First CEO Matt Clifford that provides a curated critical analysis on topics surrounding geopolitics, deep tech startups, economics and beyond.

resources.name: ML Safety Newsletter
resources.desc: A newsletter from the Center for AI Safety providing occasional deep-dives on key results in technical AI research.

resources.name: Montreal AI Ethics Institute Weekly AI Ethics newsletter
resources.desc: A weekly newsletter curated by Abhishek Gupta and his team at the Montreal AI Ethics Institute that presents accessible summaries of technical and academic research papers along with commentary on the latest in the domain of AI ethics.

resources.name: Signato
resources.desc: Weekly brief on the EU AI Act and global AI governance for HR and compliance teams. Includes a free AI Act readiness quiz.

resources.name: The Machine Learning Engineer
resources.desc: A newsletter curated by The Institute for Ethical AI & Machine Learning that contains curated articles, tutorials and blog posts from experienced Machine Learning professionals and includes insights on best practices, tools and techniques in machine learning explainability, reproducibility, model evaluation, feature analysis and beyond.
